epic.title: Baby: everything essential in the house a month before June 2027
epic.description:
First child for both Phil and Kirsty. Safety items (car seat and bases, every mattress) are bought new and the rest used or handed down; the budget is set with Kirsty after the starter lists are priced, and paid from a shared baby pot with a running total on the Family page and in the payday summary. Every list item is Need, Nice or Wait, and only Need is bought before the birth. Tickets are for decisions and jobs; the items themselves stay as rows on the Family section's three prep lists (Buying list, Nursery, Hospital bag; 0171), which keep price, link and bought. Every ticket is dated, worked back from a working due date of **2027-06-15**, with essentials in the house by **2027-05-15**. **MYC-182 asks Phil the real due date; when he answers, every date in this epic moves with it.**

## Order
The safety rules page comes first (baby.01), then pricing and the budget (baby.02), the family ask (baby.04) and three recent parents (baby.05), the pot (baby.03) and Need, Nice or Wait (baby.06). The nursery is cleared after the storage ticket (home.10, then baby.07). The comparison guides follow (car seat baby.08, pram baby.09, where the baby sleeps baby.10, cot and mattress baby.11, monitor baby.12), with the gift list (baby.35) and price watch (baby.36) built alongside. Paternity leave notice (baby.18) and Kirsty's own items (baby.20) go before the legal 15-week deadline. Big items are bought early (car seat baby.13, pram baby.14), then the nursery design (baby.15), cot and mattress (baby.16), feeding (baby.17), antenatal classes (baby.19), the monitor after the cameras network (baby.21 after net.14), the starter set (baby.23), first aid (baby.25), nursery set-up (baby.22), the nights talk (baby.28), the dry run (baby.24) and care basics (baby.26), labour support (baby.27), the house (baby.30), the done check on 2027-05-15 (baby.39), the hospital bag (baby.29), the first weeks (baby.31), the handover (baby.33) and the quiet fortnight (baby.37), then registration (baby.34) and the Wait review (baby.38). The hand-made thing (baby.32) is chosen in February.

## Done means
Everything essential in the house and set up a month before the due date (baby.39 passes).

## Flags
- 5.12 `[claude]`: the gift list is a deliberately public GET; unguessable link, items only, revocable (baby.35). Not reopened.
- 5.20 `[claude]`: tickets live in Phil's space until Kirsty joins; moving a project between spaces later re-keys its tickets (tickets-spec §17.7). Not reopened.

## Dossier
The research dossier is attached in Docs (link added by the integrator); source file `docs/run/2026-11-28/dossiers/baby.md`.

tickets.title: Safety guardrail page: a researched rules page from official UK sources (car seat law, safe sleep, mattress, monitor); each item ticket links its rule
tickets.description:
## What
Claude writes one page in Mycelium Docs titled "Baby: safety rules (official UK sources)". Each rule is numbered (R1, R2 and so on), says the rule in one line, names the source and the day it was checked. It covers at least: car seats (height-based R129 or weight-based ECE R44 labels, rear-facing until over 15 months for R129 seats, a front airbag off before any rear-facing seat in a front seat, no second-hand seat unless from family with a known history and its instructions), safe sleep (on the back, same room for at least the first six months, clear cot, 16 to 20°C with a room thermometer, no pillows, bumpers or weighted products), mattresses (new, firm, flat, waterproof cover, fits with no gaps, labelled BS EN 16890:2017+A1:2021 and BS 7177:2008+A1:2011; sleeping bags BS EN 16781:2018), cots (BS EN 716-1:2017), and monitors (no evidence they prevent sudden infant death; never a substitute for being in the room). The starting text is section 3 of the dossier `dossiers/baby.md`. Sources are only GOV.UK, the NHS, the Lullaby Trust, RoSPA's childcarseats.org.uk and BSI. When the page exists, Claude adds the matching rule numbers to baby.08, baby.09, baby.11, baby.12, baby.13, baby.14, baby.16, baby.21, baby.22, baby.24 and baby.26.

## Why
Phil: "one guardrail ticket first: a researched rules page from official UK sources; each item ticket links its rule." His worry is forgetting something essential.

## Done looks like
The Docs page exists with every rule numbered, sourced and dated, nothing from a retailer or forum, and each item ticket listed above carries a line "Rule: R…" with a link to the page.

## Unlocks
baby.02 (pricing knows which rows must be new), baby.08, baby.09, baby.10 and baby.12 (each comparison guide starts from its rules).

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Date
Worked back from the working due date of 2027-06-15. MYC-182 asks Phil the real due date; when he answers, this date moves with it.

## What

tickets.description:
## What
Phil tells his employer, in writing, the expected due date, the day he wants paternity leave to start (the birth, or a set number of days after) and whether he wants one or two weeks. GOV.UK says this must be given at least 15 weeks before the baby is expected: for a due date of Tuesday 2027-06-15 the expected week of childbirth starts Sunday 2027-06-13, and the 15th week before it runs from 2027-02-28 to Saturday 2027-03-06, so the notice must be in by 2027-03-06 at the latest. The dates of each block are confirmed at least 28 days before it starts. He also reads his employer's own policy for any enhanced pay. Only the fact the notice went in is kept here, nothing from work.

## Why
Phil: admin tickets, "paternity leave notice to work". Paternity leave is a right from the first day of employment; Statutory Paternity Pay needs 26 weeks with the employer by the end of the qualifying week (the 15th week before the due week).

## Done looks like
The written notice is sent, the date it went is in the field, and the employer's acknowledgement has come back.

## Unlocks
fin.17 (leave pay terms feed the lower-income months), baby.33 (handover before leave).

## Depends on
Nothing. The real due date from MYC-182 moves the deadline: take the Sunday on or before the due date, go back 15 weeks, and the deadline is the Saturday of that week.

## Date
Worked back from the working due date of 2027-06-15. MYC-182 asks Phil the real due date; when he answers, this date moves with it.

## What
The steps are ready before the birth and done after it. Registration: every birth in England is registered within 42 days at the register office for the area where the baby was born, or at the hospital if it offers it; take the red book and proof of identity. GP: register the baby with the family's surgery (online, through the NHS App, or the surgery's form) so the GP can book the 6 to 8 week check. tickets.title: Gift list: a shareable read-only page from the buying list, unguessable link, items only
tickets.description:
## What
Claude builds a public, read-only gift list page made from the Family prep lists. This is the one deliberately public endpoint in the plan, so its invariants are fixed: (1) the link carries a long random token (at least 128 bits from a secure random source), never a list id, space id or anything guessable, and is not listed or linked anywhere public; (2) the page shows items only: title, quantity and an optional shop link for rows the family chooses to include, and never prices, who bought what, notes, names, the due date, the space, or any other data; bought rows drop off the page; (3) it is a plain GET with no writes, no sign-in and no cookies, served with noindex and a no-referrer policy and rate-limited; (4) it is revocable: one tap on the Lists tab revokes the token, after which the old link returns a plain not-found at once, and a new link is a new token. Tests: an isolation test that a token reads only its own space's chosen rows, a test that a revoked token gives 404, and a test that no field beyond the three is ever in the response.

## Why
Phil: "Gift list: a shareable read-only page from the buying list." The flag on 5.12 records that endpoints are not public unless decided, and this one was decided: unguessable link, no personal data beyond the items.

## Done looks like
A family member can open the link on a phone and see only the chosen items; revoking it makes the link 404 straight away; the tests pass; nothing else in the app became public.

## Unlocks
Family and friends can see what is wanted; Nice rows from baby.06 are the natural candidates.

## Depends on
Nothing (it reads the existing lists). Better after baby.06 so the right rows are chosen.

## Flag
5.12 `[claude]`: this is a deliberately public GET (invariant: endpoints are not public unless decided); unguessable link, no personal data beyond the items. Decided by Phil, not reopened.

## Date
Worked back from the working due date of 2027-06-15. MYC-182 asks Phil the real due date; when he answers, this date moves with it.

## Red team

tickets.title: Price watch: alert on a real drop below a level he sets
tickets.description:
## What
Claude builds a price watch on chosen list rows: Phil sets a target price on a row that has a shop link, and he gets one push when the price is at or below the target and also below the lowest price seen in the last 90 days, so an inflated "was" price does not count as a drop. The list rows have no target-price field today, so the build adds one. Before any fetching is written, Claude checks how prices may be read without breaking a retailer's terms (a price-comparison site's own alerts read through the mail import is one route) and writes that choice on this ticket for Phil to approve.

## Why
Phil: "Price watch: yes, alert on a real drop below a level he sets." Cost is his first worry.

## Done looks like
Phil sets a target on a row; a test with a fake price feed sends exactly one push for a real drop and none for a rise or a cut from an inflated price; the reading route is approved on this ticket.
